'''Birgit Speh''' (born 1949)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2015047834.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2018-12-02.</ref> is a Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[Cornell University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.cornell.edu/birgit-speh|title=Birgit Speh|publisher=Cornell University Department of Mathematics|accessdate=August 18, 2019}}</ref> She is known for her work in [[Lie groups]], including [[Speh representation]]s (also known as Speh's representations).<ref>Sahi, Siddhartha, and [[Elias M. Stein]]. "Analysis in matrix space and Speh's representations." ''Inventiones mathematicae'' 101.1 (1990): 379-393.</ref>

==Career==
Speh received her Ph.D. from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1977.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=24495|title=Birgit Speh}}</ref> She was the first female mathematician to be given tenure by [[Cornell University]], and the first to receive the title of Professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.cornell.edu/math-women|title = Women on the Mathematics Faculty at Cornell &#124; Department of Mathematics Cornell Arts & Sciences}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

In 2012, Speh became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2015-02-10 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>  She was selected to give the 2020 AWM-AMS Emmy [[Noether Lecture]] at the 2020 [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]].<ref name="noether lecture">{{cite web |title=2020 Lecturer: Birgit Späh |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/noether-lectures/noether-lectures-2020/ |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |accessdate=14 October 2019}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Speh, Birgit; Vogan, David A. Jr. Reducibility of generalized principal series representations. ''Acta Math.'' 145 (1980)
*Speh, Birgit. Unitary representations of Gl(''n'','''R''') with nontrivial (''g'',''K'')-cohomology. ''Invent. Math.'' 71 (1983), no. 3, 443–465.
*Speh, Birgit. The unitary dual of Gl(3,'''R''') and Gl(4,'''R'''). ''Math. Ann.'' 258 (1981/82), no. 2, 113–133.
